Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark ANCHOR for engineering constraint following (10-category, 78-leaf constraint taxonomy; automated pipeline composing atomic constraints with AND/THEN/PRIORITY relations; trajectory-grounded rule + LLM judging), used to compare 19 agent configurations (2 scaffolds × 10 models) on 358 repository tasks, with and without constraints

No SDD approach evaluated. Scaffolds OpenCode and Cline (versions not given) with DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, GLM-5.1, GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.4, Kimi-K2.5, Qwen-3.5-Plus, GPT-5.4-Mini, Qwen-3.5-Flash (both scaffolds) and Claude Opus 4.8 (Cline only). Settings: constrained instruction vs task-only instruction

Benchmark instance: a natural developer instruction (short task description plus a list of constraint items; composites rendered as one item preserving AND/THEN/PRIORITY semantics) paired with a structured constraint object; evaluation checklist with, per item, a question, pass condition, judge type and evidence type (code diff, trajectory incl. final response, or commit messages). Construction uses a compressed project-context card from DeepWiki documentation

Not prescribed for the agent beyond the constraints themselves (e.g. reproduce before fix, add regression test, report commands). Benchmark construction in 5 steps: context compression, leaf selection, atomic instantiation and filtering, composite construction, query synthesis. Evaluation: checklist generation, hybrid rule/LLM judging, dependency aggregation

None in agent runs (autonomous). Humans in benchmark validation: five senior engineers audit atomic constraints of 50 instances; five evaluators label 480 checklist items to validate the LLM judge; taxonomy refined by a panel of senior software engineers
Specification format only: structured task-level engineering constraints (atomic and composite) embedded in the developer instruction, given to autonomous coding agents; no SDD workflow run

Constraint compliance: ACR (atomic compliance rate), CCR (composite/relation compliance rate), IPR (item pass rate over all checklist items), FCCR (fraction of tasks passing every checklist item); category-level Macro ACR; CCR by relation type and composite size; FCCR on task-successful vs failed trajectories; attributed error patterns E1-E6 (not perceived, misunderstood, deprioritized, capability limitation, scaffold interference, partial compliance)

Automatic: runs in isolated Docker sandboxes from a clean checkout, full interaction trace recorded; rule-based judges (path_filter, file_count, line_count, command_presence, command_arg_check, action_sequence, import_check, regex_match) and an LLM judge on evidence excerpts (judge model not named); task-bootstrap 95% CIs for category plots; error attribution by an LLM prompt. Judge validated on 480 items against majority of five human evaluators (inter-evaluator κ = 0.83; judge κ = 0.78, 89.4% agreement). Constraint audit by five engineers (Gwet AC1 0.91-0.97)

Tasks: the same 358 ANCHOR tasks for all configurations. Configurations: 19 (primary paired set 14 = 7 models × OpenCode and Cline; extended paired set 18; plus Claude Opus 4.8 under Cline). Baseline: task-only setting (same agent, original task objective without engineering constraints). Held constant: tasks, clean checkout in isolated Docker sandbox, restricted network, original test harness, 30-min timeout, checklist and judges. Acceptance: repository tests for completion; checklist judged by rules and an LLM judge. Repetitions: one run per configuration (bootstrap intervals over tasks, not repeated runs). Human intervention: none

Best: Cline + Claude Opus 4.8 (ACR 70.1, CCR 63.7, IPR 69.0, FCCR 19.0, completion 43.6); FCCR 7.0 points above Cline + GPT-5.4 (12.0). ACR exceeds CCR by 6.7 points on average. Adding constraints changes completion by +0.7 points on average in the primary set (range −4.1 to +4.5; about +0.1 over all 19). Same model, different scaffold: GPT-5.3-Codex completion 37.4 vs 37.7 but IPR 67.9 vs 62.9; GPT-5.4-Mini IPR 58.5 (OpenCode) vs 30.8 (Cline). Hardest categories: Reporting 41.0 Macro ACR, Workflow 50.1, Tool Execution 55.7, Testing 56.6; easiest Dependency 72.4. THEN hardest relation (CCR 46.7 vs AND 58.1, PRIORITY 64.0). Completion and IPR correlate (Spearman 0.87-0.91). Error attribution: E1 not perceived 38.2%, E3 deprioritized 21.9%, E6 partial 14.5%, E5 scaffold 6.9%, E4 capability 5.2%. No significance tests for configuration differences

Yes per the authors: separated constraint compliance from task completion and distinguished configurations (IPR 30.8-69.0) and scaffold-model interactions. Judge agreement with humans κ = 0.78 (0.86 rule-verifiable, 0.69 THEN/PRIORITY); ranking on the human-labelled subset Spearman 0.96 with the full judge ranking. Repeatability not assessed (single runs). Limitations stated: no cross-provider judge or prompt-sensitivity study; possible judge bias toward same-vendor models; audit covers 50 instances; gold patch visible at construction; FCCR severity-blind; small categories; differences descriptive without significance tests

Limitations: high evaluation cost; LLM judge may share biases with evaluated models, no cross-vendor judge or controlled prompt swaps; error labels are LLM interpretations, not causal; constraint audit covers only 50 instances and atomics; gold patch exposed during construction (indirect leakage possible); FCCR sensitive to any failed item and checklist size, penalizes overridden lower-priority items; category imbalance; only two open-source scaffolds, Claude Opus 4.8 only under Cline; taxonomy may miss niche domains; interactions between composites not modelled. Gaps / future work: patch-blind construction ablation, full-set audit, cross-vendor judges, applicability-aware scoring, versioned releases with contamination monitoring
